name: Soil Organic Carbon
description: Shows how much organic carbon is stored in the top 30cm of soil worldwide — the layer most affected by farming, grazing, and land use. Higher values generally mean healthier, more fertile soil. This layer is often used to track soil health and carbon loss from agriculture.

name: Protected Areas
description: Shows the boundaries of officially recognized protected areas across the world's land and oceans — national parks, marine reserves, wildlife sanctuaries, and similar. Useful for checking whether a project site, region, or piece of land overlaps with a protected area. Updated monthly with submissions from governments and conservation organizations.

name: Global Power Plants
description: Shows the location of roughly 30,000 power plants worldwide, along with the fuel type each one uses (coal, gas, hydro, solar, wind, nuclear, etc.) and how much electricity it can generate. Useful for looking at where power generation — and its associated emissions or resource use — happens across a country or region.

name: Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ)
description: This dataset shows the boundaries of each coastal country's Exclusive Economic Zone — the area extending up to 200 nautical miles from shore where that country has the right to explore, use, and manage marine resources, as set out under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.

name: GEOGLOWS 2.0 ECMWF Streamflow Model
description: This dataset shows forecasted and historical streamflow (water discharge) for over 7 million river and stream reaches worldwide, updated daily using weather data from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). Useful for spotting potential flooding, monitoring water availability, and tracking river conditions in near real time — including in places with no ground-based river gauges.
timeframe: Forecast: rolling 10-day, updated daily (3-hour intervals) · Historical simulation: 1940–present, updated weekly

name: ESA WorldCover
description: This dataset shows global land cover at 10-metre resolution, classifying the entire planet's surface into categories like cropland, forest, grassland, built-up area, and water. Detailed enough to pick out individual fields and small water bodies — useful as a base layer for land-use, deforestation, or habitat analysis.

name: Global Forest Watch — Tree Cover Loss
description: This dataset shows where forest has been lost worldwide each year since 2000, detected from satellite imagery. Useful for tracking deforestation hotspots and trends, tied to agriculture, logging, or fire, with new data added annually.
source: University of Maryland (Hansen/UMD), with Google, USGS, NASA — distributed via WRI's Global Forest Watch

name: Cropland
description: This dataset was produced for nominal 2010 by overlaying the five dominant crops of the world over the remote sensing derived global irrigated and rainfed cropland area map of the International Water Management Institute to create eight classes of crop dominance.

name: Global Human Settlement Layer (GHSL) data layers
description: This dataset shows where people live and how built-up areas have grown worldwide from 1975 to today, combining satellite imagery with census data. Useful for tracking urban growth, estimating population exposure to disasters, and classifying urban vs. rural areas using a standard UN-recommended method.
source: European Commission Joint Research Centre (EC JRC)

name: VIIRS Nighttime Lights
description: This dataset shows the intensity of nighttime lights worldwide, captured monthly by satellite. Since light output correlates with human activity, it's commonly used as an indirect proxy for economic activity, electrification, and urbanization — especially where official economic data is sparse or delayed.
source: NOAA/NCEI Earth Observation Group (hosted by Esri)

name: Gridded Livestock of the World (GLW4)
description: Shows the global density of cattle, buffalo, sheep, goats, pigs, and chickens. Useful for food security, livelihoods, health, and environmental analysis
source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

name: GPM IMERG Global Precipitation
description: Shows global precipitation estimates using observations from multiple satellites. Useful for tracking precipitation trends, extreme events, and the water cycle.
timeframe: 1998–present; updated every 30 minutes for near-real-time products

name: NASA FIRMS Active Fire Data
description: Shows active fires and thermal anomalies detected by satellites around the world. Useful for near-real-time fire monitoring and analysis.

name: Global Mangrove Watch, version 4.1 (v4.1.12)
description: Shows the global extent and change of mangrove forests. Useful for monitoring mangrove conservation and restoration.

name: Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF)
description: GBIF is an open-data infrastructure that makes biodiversity data freely available online; its database contains hundreds of millions to billions of species-occurrence records. Researchers use GBIF for species-distribution modeling, conservation planning, invasive-species research, ecological studies, and analyzing changes in biodiversity over time.

name: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List of Threatened Species
description: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species is the world's most comprehensive information source on the global conservation status and extinction risk of animal, plant and fungal species. It is managed by the IUCN and provides scientific assessments that support conservation planning, policy and biodiversity decision-making.
source: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
moreInfoLabel: IUCN Green List of Protected and Conserved Areas

name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS)
description: Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS) is a global, open-access database providing information on the distribution and occurrence of marine species and biodiversity. It is particularly relevant for your Blue Biodiversity Knowledge Explorer.

name: FAO Stat
description: FAOSTAT is a global statistical database, providing free access to food and agriculture statistics for more than 245 countries and territories. It covers areas such as crop and livestock production, food security and nutrition, trade, prices, forestry, fisheries, land use, and agricultural resources.
source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
format: Data can be explored online or downloaded in formats such as CSV, JSON, XML, and SQL, depending on the dataset. Mostly tabular / statistical data.
moreInfoLabel: Food and Agriculture Data, FAO website

name: The World Data Centre for Greenhouse Gases (WDCGG)
description: A global database of observed atmospheric concentrations of greenhouse gases and related gases, provides station-based observations and associated metadata for gases such as CO?, CH?, N?O and halocarbons.
source: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) under the WMO Global Atmosphere Watch Programme.

name: Avibase
description: A comprehensive database of the world’s bird species and subspecies, integrating taxonomic information, regional checklists, synonyms, common names, and distribution information.

name: AntWeb
description: AntWeb is a global biodiversity database specifically to ants (Formicidae), it provides specimen records, taxonomic information, high-resolution images, geographic information, and natural-history data.
source: California Academy of Sciences and GBIF

name: LandScan
description: LandScan displays the average number of people in each 1 km square across the world.

name: CHIRPS Rainfall
description: CHIRPS displays daily rainfall every five days across most of the world since 1981, from 60 degrees south to 60 degrees north.

name: FishStat
description: FishStat is FAO's global fisheries and aquaculture statistical database, providing annual, country- and species-level data on capture fisheries, aquaculture production and related fisheries statistics.
source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

name: Global Dam Watch
description: Global Dam Watch maps dams, reservoirs and other structures that block rivers around the world.

name: Poverty and Inequality Platform (PIP) estimates
description: An interactive computational tool that offers users quick access to the World Bank’s estimates of poverty, inequality, and shared prosperity
timeframe: Survey years vary by country; estimates updated periodically

name: UNAIDS HIV epidemiological estimates
description: Provides data on HIV epidemiology, programme coverage, and financing.
source: UNAIDS, with national authorities and partners

name: SRTM global elevation, version 3
description: Shows land-surface elevation measured by the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission.

name: Aqueduct Floods Hazard Maps
description: an online platform that measures riverine and coastal flood risks under both current baseline conditions and future projections in 2030, 2050, an 2080

name: GIRI (Global Infrastructure Risk Model and Resilience Index) Data Platform
description: Provides global maps and data for exploring disaster risks and infrastructure resilience.
timeframe: Existing climate conditions; future climate scenarios for 2100

name: SMAP
description: SMAP measures how much moisture is in the top layer of soil across the world every few days.

name: WAPOR
description: WaPOR measures water usage by crops and other plants.

name: Lake and Reservoir Levels
description: Measures water levels in large lakes and reservoirs

name: GEMStat
description: GEMStat collects water quality parameters from rivers, lakes and groundwater.

name: WorldClim 2.1
description: Global gridded climate data providing temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, wind speed, water vapor pressure, and bioclimatic variables.

name: TerraClimate
description: Provides a global climate and water balance at a monthly scale.

name: Koppen Geiger Climate Classification
description: Maps global climate zones, based on temperature and rainfall, that align with similar vegetation.

name: IBTrACS
description: Maps the path and strength of every recorded tropical storm, typhoon and hurricane globally.

name: Standard Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index
description: A drought index that measures moisture deficits by calculating precipitation minus potential evapotranspiration.

name: Aridity Index
description: The aridity index measures how dry a climate is by comparing rainfall with how much water could evaporate.

name: Global Drought Observatory
description: Monitors drought conditions worldwide using rainfall, soil moisture and vegetation health indices.

name: Global Homogenised Earthquake Catalogue
description: A global catalogue of earthquakes that is standardized via magnitude.

name: Active Fires
description: Monitors active fires using remote sensing data

name: Global Solar Atlas
description: Displays how much sunshine and solar generation a site can produce.

name: Global Wind Atlas
description: Displays how strong and steady the wind is at each place, and estimates how much electricity production.

name: ThinkHazard!
description: ThinkHazard! estimates the likelihood of a natural hazard at a given place from very low to high, and provides guidance on reducing those impact.

name: CITES Species+
description: The Checklist of CITES Species provides the official list of CITES-listed species and their associated scientific synonyms

name: AlgaeBase
description: AlgaeBase is a global algal database of taxonomic, nomenclatural and distributional information.

name: TRY Plant Trait Database
description: Global database of plant functional traits such as plant height, leaf area, seed mass, specific leaf area, wood density, phenology and physiological traits
source: Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry, Jena, Germany

name: Global plant functional traits
description: A global archive compiling regional plant checklists and floras, providing information on the floristic status and distribution of plant species across geographic regions. It also provides plant functional trait information.

name: SeaLifeBase
description: A global marine biodiversity database providing taxonomic, biological, ecological, distribution, habitat, life-history, and fisheries-related information for marine species.
source: Quantitative Aquatics, Inc, and the Sea Around Us at the University of British Columbia.

name: GenAge: The Ageing Gene Database
description: GenAge is a curated database of genes associated with ageing and longevity in humans and model organisms. It provides information on genes, species, gene functions, and experimental or literature evidence linking specific genes to ageing and lifespan.
source: Human Ageing Genomic Resources (HAGR), Integrative Genomics of Ageing Group

name: Botanical Information and Ecology Network (BIEN)
description: BIEN is an integrated biodiversity informatics database that combines plant occurrence records, vegetation-plot and survey data, functional trait data, taxonomic information, and species geographic-range data. It integrates records from herbaria, ecological surveys, citizen-science platforms and other botanical datasets.
source: BIEN is an integrated biodiversity informatics database/ecosystem that combines plant occurrence records, vegetation-plot and survey data, functional trait data, taxonomic information, and species geographic-range data. It integrates records from herbaria, ecological surveys, citizen-science platforms and other botanical datasets

name: Plants of the World Online (POWO)
description: POWO is a global, Kew-maintained plant biodiversity information database providing taxonomic names, synonyms, descriptions, geographic distributions, images, traits, uses and other information on the world's vascular plants.

name: Global Fishing Watch - Ocean monitoring and analysis
description: Global Fishing Watch (GFW) provides open-access geospatial datasets and data services related to global fishing activity and ocean use. It is a data platform containing multiple datasets.
moreInfoLabel: Mapping human activity at sea from space

name: AquaMaps
description: AquaMaps is a global marine biodiversity database and species-distribution mapping system. It provides standardized distribution maps for over 33,500 species of fishes, marine mammals and invertebrates.

name: FishBase
description: FishBase is a global, open-access information system on fish species, containing taxonomic, biological, ecological, distribution, fisheries and conservation-related information, it covers >33,000 fish species.
moreInfoLabel: Catalogue of Life-Find species and other Taxa by name.

name: iNaturalist
description: iNaturalist help to identify species using the database of wild species available both locally and worldwide.

name: eBird
description: eBird is an online database of bird observations providing scientists, researchers and amateur naturalists with real-time data about bird distribution and abundance.
source: Cornell Lab of Ornithology at Cornell University.

name: Catalogue of Life (COL)
description: A global catalogue of the world's known species, providing scientific names, accepted names, synonyms, taxonomic classification and species information. It is primarily a taxonomic/nomenclatural database.

name: Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS)
description: ITIS is a taxonomic database, provides standardized scientific names and taxonomic information for organisms. It includes taxonomic hierarchy, synonyms, authorship, common names, and Taxonomic Serial Numbers (TSNs), which provide unique identifiers for taxa.
source: USGS, Science for Changing World and Smithsonian Institution

name: Wikispecies
description: Wikispecies is a free, multilingual online taxonomic database that provides information on the classification and scientific names of living organisms.

name: Index Fungorum
description: Index Fungorum provides nomenclatural data for the scientific names of fungi (including yeasts, lichens, chromistan fungal analogues, protozoan fungal analogues and fossil forms) at all ranks.

name: Stockholm Convention Global Monitoring Plan (GMP) - Data Warehouse (DWH)
description: The Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants protects human health and the environment from the negative impact of toxic chemicals, and persistent organic pollutants. It covers the production, using and release of POPs from the service, unintentional production of POPs, and stockpiles and wastes containing POPs.

name: Vienna Convention - Montreal Protocol
description: Montreal Protocol is an international environmental treaty, its objective is to protect the stratospheric ozone layer by controlling and phasing out the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances (ODSs).
moreInfoLabel: Country Data-Ozone consumption of Controled substances

name: Mammal Diversity Database (MDD)
description: The Mammal Diversity Database (MDD) is a global, continuously updated database of living and recently extinct mammal species and higher taxonomic groups. It tracks taxonomic changes based on current scientific literature and provides information such as accepted names, synonyms, taxonomy, common names, type localities, and geographic distributions.
source: American Society of Mammalogists (ASM), through its Biodiversity Committee
moreInfoLabel: Track the latest taxonomic changes to living and recently extinct

name: Cropland - GFSAD30
description: Maps at the global cropland at 30 meter resolution.

name: Global Cropland Extent
description: Maps cropland change from 2000 to 2019 in four year periods.

name: Carbon Monoxide
description: Maps carbon monoxide in the air, in near real time from the burning of fuels and biomass.

name: Methane
description: Provides near real time maps of methane in the air, from wetlands, agriculture, waste and oil and gas production.

name: Explore Protected Areas (PAs) and other effective area-based conservation measures (OECMs)
description: Protected Planet is the most up to date and complete source of data on protected areas and OECMs, updated monthly with submissions from governments, non-governmental organizations, landowners and communities.

name: Globally Important Agricultural Heritage Systems (GIAHS)
description: FAO recognizes and supports traditional agricultural systems that have evolved over generations and maintain important biodiversity, landscapes, traditional knowledge, cultures, and livelihoods.
source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
format: Web-based records, HTML/text, maps, photographs, videos and documents/PDFs

name: Reptile Database
description: Global taxonomic database of living reptiles containing species classification, scientific names, synonyms, distribution, type information and literature references.
source: Maintained by Dr. Peter Uetz and Jirí Hošek, supported by photo editors, taxonomic editors, a Scientific Advisory Board, and numerous volunteers worldwide

name: World Spider Catalog (WSC)
description: A comprehensive global taxonomic database of spiders (Araneae), provides information on currently recognized spider species, genera, families, synonyms, taxonomic classifications, authorship, geographic distribution.

name: WoRMS
description: WoRMS is a global taxonomic database, it provides authoritative information on marine species names, synonyms, classification, taxonomic status, and references, covering a wide range of marine organisms.

name: International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses (ICTV)
description: ICTV is the international authority responsible for developing and maintaining the universal classification and nomenclature of viruses. It provides an authoritative taxonomy of viruses, including virus names, taxonomic ranks, and classification information.
source: International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses (ICTV)

name: Barcode of Life Data (BOLD) Systems
description: A global biodiversity database and informatics platform that stores DNA barcode sequences linked to specimen, taxonomic, geographic, and collection information. It is primarily used for species identification, DNA barcoding, biodiversity research, and monitoring.
source: Centre for Biodiversity Genomics (CBG) at the University of Guelph, Canada.
format: Tabular/TSV data for specimen and metadata records

name: Paleobiology Database
description: The Paleobiology Database (PBDB) is a global database of fossil occurrence, taxonomic, geological, and palaeobiological information. It contains geographically and geologically referenced records of organisms from different geological ages and is widely used for studying biodiversity through geological time.
source: The Paleontological Society and University of Wisconsin–Madison

name: Formaldehyde
description: Provides near-real-time maps of atmospheric formaldehyde, created when volatile organic compounds from plants, fires, traffic, and industry break down in sunlight

name: Ozone
description: The satellite maps total atmospheric ozone, including the high-altitude layer formed by sunlight and ground-level concentrations caused by pollution.

name: Nitrogen Dioxide
description: Provide near real time nitrogen dioxide in the air from shipping, traffic, powerplants and industry.

name: Sulfur Dioxide
moreInfoUrl: Provides near real time maps of sulphur dioxide in the air from power plants, smelters and volcanoes.

name: ESA CCI Global Land Cover
description: Shows what covers the land surface worldwide (forest, cropland, grassland, wetland, urban, and more) for every year since 1992. Because the maps are consistent over three decades, this layer is often used to track long-term land cover change and feed climate models.
source: ESA Climate Change Initiative / Copernicus Climate Change Service

name: Burned Area
description: Shows where fires have burned across the world and how much land burned each year, broken down by land cover type. This layer is often used to track wildfire trends, assess damage, and link fire activity to drought and land use.

name: Active Fire Detections
description: Shows fires detected by satellites as they happen, anywhere on Earth, with an archive going back two decades. This layer is often used for early warning, monitoring agricultural burning, and spotting fires linked to deforestation.

name: Historical and Projected Climate
description: Shows how temperature, rainfall, and climate extremes have changed in each country and how they are expected to change under different emissions scenarios. This layer is often used to assess climate risks to landscapes, agriculture, and development projects.

name: IPCC AR6 Regional Climate Data
description: Shows observed and projected changes in temperature, rainfall, and extremes for regions worldwide, using the data behind the latest IPCC assessment. This layer is often used as the authoritative reference for regional climate change.

name: Copernicus Climate Atlas Indices
description: Shows past and future values for climate variables and indices such as hot days, heavy rainfall, and drought conditions. This layer is often used to compare how climate hazards may change in different places.

name: Daily Global Temperature
description: Shows the world's average air and sea surface temperature each day, compared with historical averages. This dataset is often used to track record heat and communicate how fast the climate is warming.

name: Historical GHG Emissions
description: Shows how much greenhouse gas each country emits by sector, including emissions from land use change and forestry. This dataset is often used to compare countries and track progress against climate commitments (NDCs).

name: National Carbon Emissions
description: Shows each country's carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels and from land use change, along with how much carbon oceans and land absorb. This dataset is often used as the scientific reference for the global carbon balance.

name: Emissions Inventory
description: Shows estimated greenhouse gas emissions from individual sources such as power plants, farms, and forest clearing, using satellites and AI. This dataset is often used to see where emissions come from within a country, not just national totals.

name: Baseline Water Stress
description: Shows how much of the available water in each river basin is already being used. Higher values mean more competition for water and greater risk of shortages. This layer is often used to assess water risk for agriculture, cities, and investments, now and in the future.

name: Global Dynamic Land Cover
description: Shows land cover worldwide each year, including the percentage of each pixel covered by trees, shrubs, grass, crops, and other surfaces. This layer is often used where mixed landscapes matter, such as savannas and farm mosaics.

name: Dynamic World Land Cover
description: Shows near real-time land cover for every satellite pass, with the likelihood of each of nine classes such as water, trees, crops, and built-up area. This layer is often used to see recent and seasonal changes, such as flooding or crop cycles.

name: MODIS Land Cover Type
description: Shows global land cover every year since 2001 under several classification systems. Its long, consistent record makes it a standard input for land change studies and earth system models.

name: Surface Water Occurrence
description: Shows how often each location has been covered by water since 1984. Higher values mean permanent water; lower values mean seasonal or occasional flooding. This layer is often used to track shrinking lakes, new reservoirs, and wetland change.

name: Tree Cover Loss
description: Shows where trees have been removed or died each year since 2001, whether from clearing, fire, or disease. This layer is often used to monitor deforestation and to support forest policy and supply chain commitments.
source: World Resources Institute (WRI) and University of Maryland
moreInfoLabel: Global Forest Watch Open Data Portal

name: Forest Area and Change
description: Shows official country figures on how much forest each country has, how it is changing, and how much carbon it stores. This dataset is often used for national reporting and international comparisons of forest trends.
source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN (FAO)

name: Tropical Moist Forest Change
description: Shows where tropical rainforests have been cleared, degraded, or are regrowing each year since 1990. Unlike most forest maps, it separates degradation from full deforestation. This layer is often used for REDD+ and deforestation-free trade monitoring.

name: Global Mangrove Extent
description: Shows where mangrove forests grow along the world's coasts and how their extent has changed since 1996. This layer is often used for coastal protection planning, blue carbon projects, and restoration targeting.
source: Global Mangrove Alliance partners (Aberystwyth University, JAXA, and others)

name: Land Degradation Indicators
description: Shows each country's reported trends in land cover, land productivity, and soil organic carbon, the three measures of land degradation under SDG 15.3.1. This dataset is often used to track progress toward land degradation neutrality targets.

name: World Database on Protected Areas
description: Shows the boundaries of national parks, reserves, and other protected and conserved areas worldwide. This layer is often used to measure progress toward conservation targets such as 30x30 and to screen projects for environmental risk.

name: Built-Up Surface
description: Shows how much of each area is covered by buildings and how settlements have grown since 1975, with projections to 2030. This layer is often used to track urban sprawl onto farmland and natural areas.

name: Population Density
description: Shows how many people live in each small grid cell across every country. Higher values mean more densely populated areas. This layer is often used to estimate how many people depend on or are affected by a landscape, hazard, or project.

name: Indigenous and Community Lands
description: Shows lands held or used by Indigenous Peoples and local communities, including whether their rights are formally recognized. This layer is often used to respect land rights in conservation and development planning.
source: LandMark partners (WRI, Rights and Resources Initiative, and others)

name: Subnational Human Development Index
description: Shows living standards, health, and education for more than 1,700 regions within countries. Higher values mean better human development outcomes. This dataset is often used to spot regional inequality hidden in national averages.

name: Human Development Index
description: Shows each country's overall level of human development based on life expectancy, education, and income, with related gender and poverty indices. This dataset is often used for cross-country comparisons of wellbeing.

name: Gender Statistics
description: Shows how women and men compare on education, work, health, and ownership of land and assets. This dataset is often used to understand gender gaps in access to land and natural resources.

name: Acute Food Insecurity
description: Shows how severe hunger is in each area, on a five-phase scale from minimal to famine, and how many people are affected. Higher phases mean more urgent need. This dataset is often used to prioritize humanitarian response.
source: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification partnership (FAO, WFP, and others)

name: INFORM Risk Index
description: Shows each country's risk of humanitarian crisis based on hazard exposure, vulnerability, and capacity to cope. Higher scores mean greater risk. This dataset is often used to prioritize disaster preparedness and resilience investment.
source: Joint Research Centre, European Commission, and UN OCHA
moreInfoLabel: JRC / Disaster Risk Management Knowledge Centre

name: Internal Displacement
description: Shows how many people have been forced to leave their homes within their own country because of conflict or disasters such as floods and droughts. This dataset is often used to understand the human impacts of climate and land-related shocks.

name: Forest Landscape Integrity Index
description: Measures how much the world’s forests have been changed by human activity, on a scale from 0 to 10.

name: ESA CCI Global Forest Above Ground Biomass
description: Estimates forest above-ground biomass using SAR and Earth observation data.

name: Refugee Population Statistics
description: Shows the number of refugees, asylum-seekers, and other displaced people by where they come from and where they are hosted. This dataset is often used to plan support for host communities and displaced populations.

name: Travel Time to Healthcare
description: Shows how long it takes to reach the nearest healthcare facility from any location worldwide. Higher values mean more remote, underserved areas. This layer is often used to identify communities cut off from essential services.
source: Malaria Atlas Project (University of Oxford / Telethon Kids Institute)

name: Crop Suitability and Potential Yield (GAEZ v4)
description: Shows how suitable land is for growing specific crops and how much it could produce under current and future climates. Higher values mean better growing conditions. This layer is often used to plan agricultural investment and adaptation.

name: Land Cover and Land Use Statistics (FAOSTAT)
description: Shows how much land in each country is cropland, pasture, forest, and other uses, and how that has changed over decades. This dataset is often used to track agricultural expansion and compare land use across countries.
source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN (FAO)
timeframe: Land cover 1992–recent year; land use 1961–recent year

name: Forest Area (% of land area)
description: Shows the share of each country's land covered by forest over time. This indicator is often used in development reporting and to compare forest trends alongside economic data.

name: Large-Scale Land Acquisitions (Land Matrix)
description: Shows large land deals for agriculture, forestry, and mining, including who is investing, where, and how much land is involved. This dataset is often used to monitor land grabbing and investment pressure on local communities.
source: Land Matrix Initiative (ILC, CIRAD, GIGA, CDE, and others)

name: Crop Production Maps (MapSPAM)
description: Shows where more than 40 crops are grown and how much each area produces. Higher values mean more intensive production. This layer is often used to link land use to food supply and agricultural value.

name: Forest Typology
description: Shows different forest types, including natural forests, planted forests, and tree crops.

name: Global Natural Vegetation Cover
description: Maps the probability that each place would be covered by tree, shrub, or bare ground.

name: Global Forest Canopy Height
description: Measured how tall forest canopy using space based altimetry.

name: Intact Forest Landscapes
description: Map large forested area or natural areas that have no signs of human activity.

name: JRC Tropical Moist Forest
description: Maps tropical moist forest since 1999 that shows undisturbed, degraded, cleared or forest that is growing back.

name: JRC global map of forest types
description: Maps primary forest, naturally regenerating forest and plantation forest.

name: Meta/WRI Global Canopy Height
description: Maps global tree height at a one meter resolution, which supports tracking forest carbon and climate action.

name: Natural Forests of the World
description: Estimates the likelihood that an area was natural forest, rather than planted forest, tree crops or other land types.

name: Global Tree Restoration Potential
description: Maps potential tree restoration areas excluding farmland and towns using and how climate change could shift that by 2050.

name: Subnational Poverty (Geospatial Poverty Portal)
description: Shows poverty and inequality rates for provinces, states, and districts within countries, not just national averages. Higher values mean a larger share of people living in poverty. This layer is often used to target investments to the poorest regions and to overlay poverty with climate and land risks.
timeframe: Survey years vary; harmonized to common years

name: Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)
description: Shows how many people are poor across health, education, and living standards at the same time, for countries and their regions. Higher values mean deeper, overlapping deprivation. This dataset is often used to see poverty that income measures miss, especially in rural areas.
source: Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and UNDP

name: World Population Prospects
description: Shows past, present, and projected population for every country, including age structure, births, deaths, and migration. This dataset is often used to anticipate future pressure on land, food, and services.
source: UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA)

name: Urban Indicators and Slum Population
description: Shows the share of city dwellers living in slums or informal settlements, along with other urban indicators such as access to open space. Higher values mean more people in inadequate housing. This dataset is often used for urban planning and SDG 11 reporting.

name: Drinking Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (JMP)
description: Shows the share of people with access to safe drinking water, sanitation, and handwashing facilities, split by urban and rural areas. Lower values mean greater unmet need. This dataset is often used to target WASH investments and to track SDG 6.
source: WHO and UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP)

name: Access to Electricity and Clean Cooking (Tracking SDG7)
description: Shows the share of people with electricity and with clean cooking fuels in each country. Low clean cooking access often means heavy reliance on firewood and charcoal, a driver of forest degradation. This dataset is often used to link energy access to land and forest pressure.
source: World Bank (ESMAP), IEA, IRENA, UN Statistics Division, and WHO

name: Food Security Indicators (FAOSTAT)
description: Shows the prevalence of undernourishment and of moderate or severe food insecurity in each country, along with dietary and access indicators. Higher values mean more people struggle to get enough food. This dataset is often used for SDG 2 tracking and the annual State of Food Security report.
source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN (FAO)

name: Employment in Agriculture (ILOSTAT)
description: Shows the share of workers employed in agriculture, forestry, and fishing in each country, by sex. Higher values mean livelihoods depend more directly on land. This dataset is often used to understand who is affected by land degradation and land use change.

name: Land Tenure Security Perceptions (Prindex)
description: Shows the share of adults who fear losing their land or home, by country and by group such as women and renters. Higher values mean people feel less secure in their rights. This dataset is often used to design land governance and tenure programs.

name: Conflict Events (UCDP Georeferenced Event Dataset)
description: Shows the location, date, and death toll of individual organized violence events worldwide. This dataset is often used to understand how conflict overlaps with land, resources, and fragile landscapes.
source: Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP), Uppsala University

name: Disaster Impacts (EM-DAT)
description: Shows recorded disasters worldwide since 1900, including floods, droughts, storms, and landslides, with deaths, people affected, and economic losses. This dataset is often used to track how climate-related hazards affect people over time.
source: Centre for Research on the Epidemiology of Disasters (CRED), UCLouvain
